original_statement:
What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. type_lint reports no layerDiscipline finding for shield_can_happen. The statement of shield_can_happen does not change.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. At integrated, scripts/type_lint.lean prints a layerDiscipline finding with declaration shield_can_happen.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. Run `lake build ArmadaLean ArmadaLean.Lint.TypeDoctrine` and `lake env lean scripts/type_lint.lean` through /home/rix/bin/lean-run; read the JSON lines by their linter and declaration fields.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. No spec statement changes; scripts/check.sh --json reports signatures_ok true. scripts/check.sh --json keeps every _ok field true against scripts/gate-baseline.json; a full run takes up to 1500 seconds. When a count falls, scripts/update_gate_baseline.py rewrites the baseline in the same branch. A bare `lake clean` is never run.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) shield_can_happen
restatement: Fix the Lean proof of shield_can_happen so that the type-doctrine linter (scripts/type_lint.lean) no longer reports a layerDiscipline finding for that declaration, meaning the proof must stop unfolding a base operation it should treat opaquely. The formal statement (type signature) of shield_can_happen must remain exactly as it is — only the proof may change. After the fix, running `lake build ArmadaLean ArmadaLean.Lint.TypeDoctrine` followed by `lake env lean scripts/type_lint.lean` via /home/rix/bin/lean-run must produce JSON lint lines with no layerDiscipline entry whose declaration field is shield_can_happen. Additionally, scripts/check.sh --json must report signatures_ok true, and every _ok field in its JSON output must remain true relative to scripts/gate-baseline.json (unless a count falls, in which case scripts/update_gate_baseline.py updates the baseline in the same branch). A full check.sh run may take up to 1500 seconds. Under no circumstances should a bare `lake clean` be run, since it would destroy the shared Mathlib build used by all worktrees.

goal: Make an automated code-quality check stop flagging one specific proof for breaking a layering rule, without altering what that proof claims to prove, and without breaking any other existing checks or accidentally wiping shared build artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Running the project's type-doctrine linter should produce no layer-discipline warning about the proof named shield_can_happen. A person can see this by checking that the lint report lists zero such findings for that proof.

Confirms that the declared type of shield_can_happen in the Lean source has not been edited, by printing the exact signature line found in the codebase and checking it matches the original expected signature.
Running the project's check script with the --json flag should print a report where the signatures_ok field is true, confirming that all function signatures match their expected declarations.

Running the project's check script and asking it for JSON output shows that every field ending in '_ok' reads true, meaning all quality gates (lint, decision scope, etc.) pass and nothing has regressed below the recorded baseline.
Running the project's full check script from start to finish should complete within 1500 seconds, as shown by timing the run and reporting how long it took.
Checks the record of shell commands run during the work to confirm that no one ever typed a bare `lake clean` (which would wipe out the shared Mathlib build used by every worktree).
